title: LengthDelimitedCodec Builder doc examples (new/new_codec/new_read/new_write) still use broken length_adjustment(0)+num_skip(0) combo, corrupts frames
body:
LengthDelimitedCodec Builder doc examples (new/new_codec/new_read/new_write) still use broken length_adjustment(0)+num_skip(0) combo, corrupts frames
Version
tokio-util 0.7.19, rustc 1.97.1, tokio-rs/tokio commit dd344a5
Description
Four Builder method doc examples in tokio-util/src/codec/length_delimited.rs show .length_adjustment(0) combined with .num_skip(0) as a working configuration:


Builder::new — lines 677-690


Builder::new_codec — lines 951-961


Builder::new_read — lines 977-990


Builder::new_write — lines 1002-1017
LengthDelimitedCodec::builder()
.length_field_offset(0)
.length_field_type::()
.length_adjustment(0)   // default value
.num_skip(0)
.new_read(io);


This combination silently corrupts decoded frames: num_skip(0) means the length-header bytes are never advanced past, but length_adjustment(0) does not compensate by adding the header width back into the byte count that gets sliced off. The result is a decoded frame that includes the raw header bytes at the front and is short at the back, with the missing tail bytes leaking into the next frame's header.
Reproduction
let mut codec = LengthDelimitedCodec::builder()
    .length_field_offset(0)
    .length_field_type::<u16>()
    .length_adjustment(0)
    .num_skip(0)
    .new_codec();

let mut buf = BytesMut::new();
codec.encode(Bytes::from_static(b"hello world"), &mut buf).unwrap();
let frame = codec.decode(&mut buf).unwrap();
assert_eq!(frame, Some(BytesMut::from(&b"hello world"[..]))); // fails

Actual decoded output: b"\0\x0bhello wor" (header bytes prepended, "ld" truncated and left in the buffer to corrupt the next frame). Expected: b"hello world".
This isn't caught by the doctests because they are compile-only (no assert/round-trip executed) — confirmed via cargo test --doc --all-features.
Why this matters
These are the canonical examples a developer copies when first configuring LengthDelimitedCodec::Builder. Copying new_codec/new_read/new_write as shown produces a codec that silently corrupts every frame after the first.
Prior history
This exact corruption mechanism was reported in #6604 and closed by #6638 (merged 2024-06-14). However, #6638 only fixed the module-level "Example 1–6" walkthroughs earlier in the file — it never touched these four Builder::* method-doc examples, which still contain the identical broken snippet on current master.
Suggested fix
Apply the same fix #6638 used elsewhere in this file: either drop .num_skip(0) (falls back to the default skip-header behavior, matching Example 1), or add .length_adjustment(2) to account for the 2-byte u16 header width — and make the doctest actually execute and assert a round-trip, as #6638 did for the module-level examples.
Suggested labels: T-docs, A-tokio-util

tokio 1.53.0 breaks its declared MSRV (1.71) on Windows: OnceLock::wait (Rust 1.86) in signal/windows/sys.rs
body:
Version
tokio v1.53.0 (crates.io, published 2026-07-17)
Platform
Windows (x86_64-pc-windows-msvc) — the affected code is behind cfg(windows); other platforms are unaffected.
Description
tokio 1.53.0 declares rust-version = "1.71" in its manifest, but src/signal/windows/sys.rs:112 (at tag tokio-1.53.0) calls OnceLock::wait:
let Ok(registry) = REGISTRY.wait().as_ref() else {
OnceLock::wait was stabilized in Rust 1.86, so any Windows build of tokio 1.53.0 with a toolchain in the declared-supported range 1.71..1.86 fails:
error[E0599]: no method named `wait` found for struct `OnceLock` in the current scope
   --> tokio-1.53.0/src/signal/windows/sys.rs:112:33
    |
112 |     let Ok(registry) = REGISTRY.wait().as_ref() else {
    |                                 ^^^^ method not found in `OnceLock<Result<Registry, i32>>`

I expected cargo check with any toolchain ≥ the declared rust-version to succeed; instead it fails on Windows for every toolchain below 1.86. Since the code path is cfg(windows)-gated, I suspect the MSRV CI job doesn't cover the Windows signal module.
Observed in the wild: this began breaking downstream MSRV CI on Windows the day 1.53.0 published (e.g. open-telemetry/opentelemetry-rust's msrv (windows-latest) job, verifying an example against Rust 1.75 — failing job, diagnosis in open-telemetry/opentelemetry-rust#3599 (comment)).
(Disclosure: this report was drafted with AI assistance; the source facts — the tag's manifest rust-version, the sys.rs call site, and the publish date — were verified directly against the tokio-1.53.0 tag and crates.io.)

tokio-stream: consider restoring cooperative budgeting in `iter`
body:
Summary
tokio_stream::iter currently has an explicit TODO: add coop back and uses a local yield_amt counter to return Poll::Pending after every 32 yielded items.
Would it make sense to restore integration with Tokio's cooperative budgeting when the relevant Tokio runtime feature is available, while keeping the current simple fallback for configurations without it?
Context
Current implementation:

tokio-stream/src/iter.rs stores yield_amt on Iter<I>.
poll_next increments the counter on each yielded item.
Once the counter reaches 32, it resets the counter, wakes the current task, and returns Poll::Pending.
The code has an explicit comment: // TODO: add coop back.

This is not necessarily a correctness bug: a Stream is allowed to return Pending and later produce more items. The concern is more about scheduler integration and maintainability.
Motivation
The current implementation effectively gives tokio_stream::iter its own hard-coded cooperative-yield policy. That seems slightly separate from Tokio's broader cooperative scheduling machinery.
Using Tokio's cooperative budget where available could:

keep fairness behavior aligned with the runtime's existing coop mechanisms;
avoid a standalone magic number in this adapter;
make behavior easier to reason about alongside other budget-aware Tokio primitives;
potentially make runtime metrics and forced-yield behavior more consistent.

Possible approach
One possible direction:

under the appropriate Tokio rt/coop-enabled configuration, use Tokio's cooperative budget mechanism in poll_next;
preserve the current lightweight fallback behavior where coop is not available;
keep the public API and item semantics unchanged.

Suggested tests
Before changing behavior, it would be useful to add focused tests for:

a large finite iterator does not starve a sibling task under a Tokio runtime;
size_hint continues to delegate to the underlying iterator;
EOF behavior around the current 32-item boundary does not rely on an extra spurious pending poll;
behavior remains sensible when Tokio runtime features are not enabled.

Question
Is restoring coop integration for tokio_stream::iter still desirable, or is the current manual yield_amt behavior now the intended design?
If the former, I would be happy to work on a small PR following maintainer guidance.

In tokio exists the JoinSet. It can be consumed through multiple calls to join_next(). But it can’t be consumed as a Stream. I understand tokio don’t depend on futures which explains why no Stream are exposed. But tokio_stream seems to fill this hole by providing wrappers (for example, tokio::mpsc::Receiver has a corresponding tokio_stream::wrappers::ReceiverStream).

I suppose we could expose a tokio_stream::wrappers::JoinSetStream that would implement Stream.

title: tokio-util write_all_vectored can drop data after partial vectored writes
body:
Description
tokio_util::io::write_all_vectored can advance the provided IoSlice list incorrectly after a partial poll_write_vectored result. The local advance_slices helper removes fully written buffers, then re-slices the new first buffer with &first[..left]. At that point, left is the number of bytes already consumed from that buffer, so the helper keeps the written prefix instead of the unwritten suffix.
Example
For buffers [b"ab", b"cd"], if poll_write_vectored returns 2, the helper removes the first buffer and then replaces b"cd" with b"cd"[..0]. The future then sees no non-empty buffers and returns Ok(()), silently dropping b"cd".
For buffers [b"hello", b"world"], if poll_write_vectored returns 3, the helper resumes from b"hel" instead of b"lo", so subsequent writes can duplicate already-written bytes and skip unwritten bytes.
Expected behavior
After a partial vectored write, write_all_vectored should continue from the unwritten suffix of the current buffer, and should continue with the next buffer when the write count lands exactly on a buffer boundary.
Suggested fix
Change the helper to retain &first[left..], and add regression coverage for a partial write inside a buffer and an exact buffer-boundary write.

title: Notify::notify_one has priority on Notify::notify_waiters
oneshot retains rx_task waker even after rx is closed, leads to RawTask 'leak'
body:
https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/blob/master/tokio/src/sync/oneshot.rs#L1301
The rx_task waker is only used if the oneshot is not closed. Therefore, I think it would be reasonable to uninitialise the rx_task waker on close. Because we do not currently do this, we hold a reference to the receiving-end task waker for no reason, and this can lead to a RawTask memory leak; even after cancellation, the RawTask containing the receive-side future is kept around as long as the oneshot sender still exists. Obviously this can be fixed by dropping any closed senders, but it is very unintuitive that this can lead to a task leak on the receiving side (and tasks are quite large, while the oneshot inner is typically small, so the task leak would dominate).
If we agree this is a sensible change I would love to make the PR!
